- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 2–4% to align with sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings sharply.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overpredicts; apply 2–4% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average sentiment is >0.0.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply 1–3% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model tends to lag; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
